digest.component_or_area: fsck snapshot rebuild and event compaction
propositions: rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log replays only surviving event files after pre-Jul-7 compaction deleted folded source events, causing status changes that existed only in SNAPSHOT compiled_state to be permanently lost

rebar fsck --repair silently rewrote 214 closed tickets (194 to in_progress, 20 to open) and dropped 480 events total when rebuild was triggered by orphan detection, because the fail-closed guard gated only trigger classification not rebuild blast radius

rebuild cannot distinguish between a ticket whose log is legitimately complete versus one where pre-snapshot events were deleted, so it unconditionally replays surviving files and loses any history not present on disk
--dry-run flag is ignored on fsck --repair-snapshots path (fsck.py:582) causing mutations when read-only preview was intended
505 live tickets have snapshots citing source_event_uuids with no corresponding files on disk due to legacy delete-style compaction, making them vulnerable to the same silent history loss
deleted event files remain recoverable from git history at the deleting commit's parent, allowing automatic restoration of missing sources as .retired files to complete the log before rebuild
